title: AI Coders Scored 17% Lower—Here's What They Did Wrong
summary: Short explainer of Anthropic's study: AI-assisted learners scored lower, with outcomes depending on usage pattern.

assertions.quote: Developers using AI scored 17% lower on skill tests

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 RCT found AI-assisted learners scored lower on mastery of a new library, and other studies show reduced engagement; effects depend on how AI is used.
The review describes 'cognitive debt': deferring understanding during fast iteration raises later debugging and maintenance costs. It does not measure skill loss directly.

assertions.quote: The lowscoring patterns all have one thing in common. You stop thinking

verdicts.note: Anthropic's 2026 study found high scorers used AI for conceptual questions and explanations while low scorers delegated; small sample and a single learning task.

assertions.quote: it makes good developers better. It doesn't make beginners good

verdicts.note: Experts get more reliable results and catch errors, but several RCTs show larger measured speedups for juniors, and METR found experts slowed; contested.
